## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the US tariff on lithium-ion batteries?

Lithium-ion batteries are classified under HTS 8507.60 with a base duty rate of 3.4%. Section 301 tariffs on Chinese-origin lithium-ion batteries add 25%, bringing the effective rate to 28.4% for Chinese imports.

### Are EV batteries subject to additional tariffs? [...] Yes, EV battery cells and packs from China face Section 301 tariffs of 25% on top of the base 3.4% duty. This has accelerated battery production shifts to South Korea, Japan, and domestic US facilities.

### What HTS code is used for batteries?

Batteries fall under HTS 8507 (electric accumulators). Lithium-ion is 8507.60, lead-acid is 8507.10, nickel-metal hydride is 8507.50. Each has different base duty rates ranging from 2.7% to 3.4%.

results.title: HS Code for Batteries (US)
results.content:
Batteries are split between two HTS headings: 8506 covers \\primary\\ (non-rechargeable) batteries (alkaline, lithium primary, manganese dioxide), and 8507 covers \\secondary\\ (rechargeable) batteries: lead-acid, nickel-metal hydride, lithium-ion, and others. Lithium-ion batteries (8507.60) are the most economically significant subheading because they cover laptops, phones, EV traction packs, power tools, and grid storage. General MFN rates range from 2.5% to 3.5% across the heading. Battery [...] The \\lithium-ion EV vs other split\\ at 8507.60.00.10 vs.20 matters for both rate (same 3.4% MFN, but Section 301 stacking differs) and statistical reporting under recent EV-related trade measures.

A practical note: batteries integrated into a finished device (a laptop with a built-in battery, a power tool with a battery pack) generally follow the parent device's classification. Standalone batteries (including OEM replacements and aftermarket packs) classify under 8506 / 8507. [...] 3Skipping the EV-vs-other suffix split at 8507.60.00; EV traction packs (.10) and other lithium-ion (.20) share the same MFN rate but have different Section 301 / IRA exposure.

4Treating batteries integrated into a finished device as standalone batteries; a laptop with a built-in battery is classified as a laptop (8471), not split out under 8507.

results.content:
Ironically, the electric vehicles these Li-Ion batteries power are yet to be given their own HS code. EVs are covered by the all-purpose “Motor Vehicles – Other” code of HS 8703.90.00. The World Customs Organization has proposed a separate code for EVs as part of the next round of HS revisions in 2017. Look for the US to adopt the revised codes – and for more precise data on trade in EVs – a year earlier, in 2016.

results.title: Tariffs on critical minerals and their role in the electric ...
results.content:
## Tariffs and tariff escalation

Tariffs on products related to the EV value chain can vary across different processing stages and between economies. In general, the tariffs on battery packs and EVs are considerably higher than those on raw minerals and battery minerals, with a clear pattern of tariff escalation moving up the value chain. Figure 1 summarizes the tariffs applied by economies at different levels of development on critical minerals throughout the EV value chain. [...] The EV value chain for cobalt, graphite and lithium consists of five stages: extraction of raw minerals, processing of minerals, production of electrodes for batteries, manufacturing of batteries, and production of EVs (see Table 1). Trade flows for critical minerals occur at each stage of this value chain.

Table 1: Stages for critical minerals in the EV value chain and corresponding Harmonized System (HS) codes [...] The shift towards clean energy technologies and electric vehicles (EVs) is gaining momentum as the world seeks to combat climate change. This transition requires increased use of critical minerals, such as cobalt, graphite and lithium, which are essential components of EV batteries. However, the use of escalating tariffs in EV production chains could be a factor preventing developing economies from diversifying their exports and moving up the value chain.
